walkthroughs.body_html:
Food, Nutrition and Health — a core area of GCSE Food Technology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Food, Nutrition and Health brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Food, Nutrition and Health.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What are the 4 Cs of food hygiene?
options: Calories, Carbs, Calcium, Cholesterol.
Cleaning, Cooking, Chilling, and avoiding Cross-contamination.
Chopping, Cleaning, Cooling, Carrying.
The food is organic.

mcqs.q: On a traffic-light label, what does a red light indicate?
options: High amounts of that nutrient per 100g - eat less often.
The food is dangerous and should never be eaten.
Because they are illegal.
The food is organic.

mcqs.q: Why must the 14 major allergens be highlighted on UK food labels?
options: To advertise that the food contains them.
Because they are illegal.
Reactions can be severe or life-threatening, so consumers must identify them at a glance.
Calories, Carbs, Calcium, Cholesterol.
